paragraphs: Droplet sells document automation software built for education, replacing paper forms and the approvals that trail behind them. More broadly, the company describes itself as a platform for any organization swapping manual processes for online forms and workflow automation.

Staff build forms for things like permission slips, reimbursement requests, HR paperwork and facility work orders. Conditional logic tailors what each person sees, and the company counts more than 100 component configurations. Rules-based routing then sends each submission where it belongs, by department, account code or location. An electronic signature feature collects legally binding signatures and shows in real time who has signed. An existing PDF can be dragged in and turned into a digital form.

The company says over 250 school districts use it. Departments named run from finance, HR and IT to transportation, nutrition, facilities and student services. On compliance, the company states that it meets FERPA, SOC 2 and data privacy requirements schools face. Its company page names Pelion Venture Partners among its backers.
